title: Noetherian irreducible cohomology vanishing
statement: Let X be an irreducible Noetherian topological space, let d be a nonnegative integer with dim X <= d [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let F be an abelian sheaf on X. Then H^q(X,F) [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] is zero for every integer q>d.

proof.text: Induct on d with the assertion quantified over all Noetherian spaces of dimension at most d, all abelian sheaves, and all degrees q>d; the empty-space case follows from the empty-cover sheaf axiom.
In the irreducible d=0 case every nonempty open is X, so F is the constant sheaf F(X), and irreducible constant-sheaf acyclicity gives vanishing above zero.

For d>0, Noetherianity verifies the first three hypotheses of 02UX. For a quasi-compact open U, the empty case is zero; otherwise Z=X\U is Noetherian of dimension at most d-1. The open-closed sequence for the constant sheaf and closed-immersion comparison give the exact segment H^(q-1)(Z,Z_Z) -> H^q(X,j_!Z_U) -> H^q(X,Z_X), whose outer terms vanish by outer induction and constant acyclicity because q-1>d-1.

All four hypotheses of 02UX give the irreducible result at the fixed bound d. Extend this to all Noetherian spaces at d by induction on their finite number of irreducible components: zero components is the empty case, one component uses the irreducible result just established, and otherwise choose a component Z and put U=X\Z and Zprime=closure(U), the union of the remaining components. Both closed subspaces are Noetherian, have dimension at most d, and have fewer components. The open-closed sequence expresses its outer terms as closed pushforwards from Z and Zprime; component induction, closed-pushforward cohomology comparison, and the long exact sequence kill H^q(X,F). This completes the outer dimension induction without applying the all-dimensions component theorem.
